name: Yang Kuei-fei
bio: Yang Kuei-fei (Yang Guifei, 719-756) was the imperial concubine of the T'ang emperor Ming Huang, remembered as the "White Poplar" beauty of his court. The date above is the one Ayscough and Lowell's Contents gives.
The archive holds one poem from Fir-Flower Tablets (1921), a poem of a dance, set down as four brief pictures.

poems.title: Dancing
poems.author: Yang Kuei-fei
poems.note: In the book: the "White Poplar" imperial concubine of the Emperor Ming Huang.
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
Wide sleeves sway.
Scents,
Sweet scents
Incessantly coming.

It is red lilies,
Lotus lilies,
Floating up,
And up,
Out of Autumn mist.

Thin clouds
Puffed,
Fluttered,
Blown on a rippling wind
Through a mountain pass.

Young willow shoots
Touching,
Brushing,
The water
Of the garden pool.
